summary: Completed Phases 1-10 of the 15-phase plan. This continuation dispatch completed Phase 7 (agent-system/extensions/literature/, 94->0), Phase 8 (remaining ten agent-system extensions -- cslib, email, formal, founder, lean, memory, nix, nvim, present, web -- 122->0; agent-system/extensions/ now scans clean at 0 across its entirety), Phase 9 (lua/**, 32->0, all 13 modules verified to still load headlessly), and Phase 10 (.memory/**, 18->0, discovering and documenting a new Exemption Taxonomy Category 7 for memory-vault frontmatter provenance fields, marked in place with inline # task-ref-ok YAML comments rather than rewritten). Repo-wide total dropped from 876 to 610 occurrences, all of which now live exclusively within .opencode/** (Phases 11-14). Phase 15 (blocking hook flip, strictly last) remains gated on all four trees reporting 0 via the unscoped scan.
continuation_path: Resume at Phase 11 (.opencode/extensions/core/, 199 occurrences per the plan's Scope Hypothesis -- re-confirm live since .opencode has drifted from agent-system/extensions/core, it is not a byte-copy). Run REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/check-task-references.sh --quiet .opencode/extensions/core to see the live findings scoped to that tree. CRITICAL: .opencode/** is a git-tracked, hand-maintained port -- it is NEVER generated from agent-system/ and must be edited DIRECTLY IN PLACE, never routed through agent-system/. Phases 11-14 are territory-disjoint (Phase 11: extensions/core/; Phase 12: the other eight .opencode extensions; Phase 13: context/{core,formats}/; Phase 14: everything else under .opencode/) and may run in any order or in parallel. Phase 15 MUST run last, strictly gated on the UNSCOPED check-task-references.sh (no PATH_SCOPE argument) exiting 0 across all four trees -- do not touch Phase 15 until that gate passes for real.
decisions_made: Category 7 added to the Exemption Taxonomy in rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md during Phase 10: 'Memory vault frontmatter provenance fields (topic, source)'. These are written directly by memory-harvest.sh (topic: "task-${task_number}") and /learn as structured provenance data, not deliverable prose -- a placeholder would falsify which task actually produced the memory. Resolved by marking the 15 affected frontmatter lines in place with an inline `# task-ref-ok inline, category 7 (memory frontmatter provenance field)` YAML comment (verified via yaml.safe_load round-trip that field values are byte-for-byte unchanged), rather than rewriting the values. Only the memory PROSE BODY is purged normally; the frontmatter block is marked, never rewritten, for this rule.

Two MEM-*.md files (MEM-config-nextcord-discord-nixos.md, MEM-insight-opencode-headless-cli-api.md) had a source: field with a redundant 'Task 547: ' prose prefix in front of the actual specs path -- this prefix was dropped rather than marked, since the harvest template's real shape (memory-harvest.sh line ~131) is a bare path with no prefix, so dropping it doesn't misrepresent the field's intended semantics the way rewriting a topic: "task-NNN" value would.

cslib's lint-fix-wave-assignment.md is a full case-study document built entirely around two real historical task numbers (210, 211) as its central worked example, including a git-worktree code example using those numbers in directory/branch/patch names. Followed the same case-naming convention Phase 4 used for the BimodalLogic task-273 baseline: renamed to 'the rename task' / 'the keyword-change task' throughout prose, and to cslib-renames/cslib-keywordchanges + renames.patch/keywordchanges.patch in the worktree code example.

email's context/project/email/context/project/email/design/email-to-memory-preferences.md had FOUR 'task 823' citations that were all forward-looking (the doc recommends spawning a follow-up task, not citing an existing one) -- converted to 'a future follow-up task' rather than a backward-looking durable anchor, since no such task exists yet to name.

email-preferences.md's 'Task 72' (cited 4 times, including in the document's own title) is a genuine citation of this repo's own real task and is the load-bearing anchor for what the whole document calls 'the aerc-tagged model' -- given the descriptive name 'the aerc-tagged JSONL-manifest unsubscribe-review model' and reused identically at every citation site, including the title. Its separate '`~/Mail` tasks 014/022/023' citation is a DIFFERENT, unrelated cross-repo tracker (a discarded prior-art approach) and was generalized to 'an earlier `~/Mail`-repo approach' rather than given a case name, since it is mentioned only once as a discard rationale.

founder/commands/project.md already used {N} placeholder convention consistently throughout its own Workflow Summary section except for one stray concrete '/project 234' example -- converted that one site to match the file's own established convention rather than introducing a new marker, since the file already demonstrates the placeholder pattern is sufficient there.

memory extension's three usage-guide docs (learn.md, knowledge-capture-usage.md, learn-usage.md) use '/learn --task 142'-style examples as genuine command-usage documentation (Category 3: the flag takes a real number). These were wrapped in task-ref-ok:begin/end blocks covering the full illustrative walkthrough (command + narrative + sample output), not converted to placeholders, since Category 3 explicitly keeps concrete numbers for usability.

which-key.lua and cli.lua (lua/**) both had pre-existing uncommitted user changes unrelated to this task at Phase 9 start. which-key.lua's task-73 citation fix was isolated via a manually-constructed single-hunk git apply --cached patch, keeping the unrelated CloseOtherBuffers fix out of the Phase 9 commit. cli.lua's task-851 citation sat inside a single atomic insertion hunk (temp diagnostic instrumentation) that could not be split at sub-line granularity without disproportionate patch surgery for a one-line comment fix -- that whole hunk was staged as part of the Phase 9 commit (recorded as a deviation in phase-9-progress.json).
dead_ends: check-task-references.sh's PATH_SCOPE argument only accepts directory paths, not individual file paths -- for a single-file verification, cross-check with plain grep/awk instead (still true, carried forward from the prior continuation).

Do not attempt to research the specific historical task behind every recurring 'task N' citation before converting it -- dropping the number (or reusing an already-established anchor phrase) is correct and fast when surrounding prose already states the mechanism. Only genuinely central case-study documents (cslib's lint-fix-wave-assignment.md, email-preferences.md's Task 72) warranted a full descriptive case-name treatment reused at every citation site.
